Subject: SLA-driven service-path qualification: Hosted vs Dedicated follow-up

Hi Maya / Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call focused on deciding whether QuickCart should start on Redwood Hosted API or move straight to Dedicated capacity:

- Observed traffic patterns you shared: 10–15 reqs/sec average, 200–300 concurrent short sessions during peak promos (local peak ~1.2k rps for burst window).
- Target latency: p95 <= 120ms for 64-token prompt + 128-token response (tight for a hosted setup without reserved capacity).
- Quality/consistency needs: low variance during promotions; willingness to accept brief failover to alternate smaller models for cost control.

For clarity I put together a simple SLA-driven matrix (attached qc-performance-matrix.csv) that maps throughput/latency bands to recommended service paths: Hosted (fast time-to-value), Dedicated (predictable p95 under heavy bursts), Private (only if you need VPC/on-prem or strict residency).

Suggested next steps:
1) Quick telemetry request — can you share 48h token-size distribution and a 7-day QPS histogram? This will let us size a realistic Dedicated config and benchmark a Hosted pilot.
2) Minimal pilot proposal — 2 weeks comparing Hosted with a Dedicated reserved instance (we’ll run synthetic and recorded traffic replay). I attached a pilot scope (qc-pilot-scope.xlsx) with the test plan and success criteria.
3) Pricing sketch — I’ll send an initial price comparison once we get the telemetry.

If you’re comfortable, I’ll schedule a 30-min working session early next week to lock the telemetry fields and timeline.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: qc-pilot-scope.xlsx, qc-performance-matrix.csv]
